src/domain/task-status.ts: taskStatuses tuple and TaskStatus type are the single source of status values; asTaskStatus is the only status validation
src/domain/errors.ts: DomainError base with NotFoundError, ValidationError, ConflictError subclasses used across entities.ts and task-status.ts
src/domain/repositories.ts: UserRepository, ProjectRepository, TaskRepository, IdGenerator ports typed against domain entities and TaskStatus (TaskFilters.status)

parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The src/domain module passes. All four files cover one concern, the task-management domain model:
- entities.ts holds the entities (User, Project, Task).
- errors.ts holds the domain error hierarchy (DomainError and its subclasses).
- task-status.ts holds the TaskStatus value type and its validation.
- repositories.ts holds the persistence and ID-generation ports.

The module uses its own abstractions consistently:
- Every entity validates text through the shared private helper requiredText.
- Every failure is raised as a DomainError subclass (ValidationError, ConflictError).
- TaskStatus is defined once, from the taskStatuses tuple, and reused in Task and TaskFilters.

Each rule lives in one place. Status values and the check that a status is valid exist only in task-status.ts. The rule for required text exists only in requiredText. The 'already done' check exists only in Task.markDone.

Two minor points don't break cohesion:
- The asTaskStatus error message spells out the status names instead of building them from taskStatuses.
- IdGenerator sits in repositories.ts, but it is still a domain port.
